object_description: a ground-floor gym, four-story school bar, and pentagonal extension
design_condition: The buildings form an ensemble around the sports field, address the street with a widened school volume, and preserve a forested river edge, although the occupied site leaves little room for future development.

positive.statement: The differentiated situation proposal integrates the large-scale buildings and the neighborhood context appropriately.

position.rationale: Distinct gym, school bar, and pentagonal volume visibly form a differentiated ensemble.

positive.statement: The gym roof creates an appropriate scale toward the sports field and references the town hall architecture.

position.rationale: The lower western gym mass has a distinct roof profile toward the open field.

positive.statement: The sports field with its street-side grandstand acts as a unifying outdoor element.

position.rationale: The south-side open edge is the plausible sports-field and grandstand zone.

positive.statement: The organization of the gym is well thought out, with versatile use and naturally lit access spaces.

position.rationale: The low western volume is used as the gym and naturally lit access anchor.

positive.statement: The proposed school structure promises flexible and therefore sustainable use.

position.rationale: The elongated four-story bar visibly provides the primary school structure.

positive.statement: The location of the new buildings integrates the town hall and the existing small building into an ensemble with connections beyond the perimeter.

position.target: ensemble with connections beyond the perimeter
position.rationale: The building cluster and perimeter connections are represented around the central ensemble.

positive.statement: The project is economically viable overall.

position.rationale: Economic judgment has no useful spatial referent.

negative.statement: Geometric requirements and topographical conditions do not allow the proposed ground-floor gym and external ramp solution.

position.rationale: The low south-west edge represents the constrained gym and ramp condition.

negative.statement: Public use of the outdoor spaces is possible only to a limited extent because they are mostly reserved for school operations.

position.target: outdoor spaces reserved for school operations
position.rationale: South-side open areas around the sports complex represent restricted public use.

negative.statement: The outsourced auditorium is less suitable for day-to-day school operations because it is decoupled from the school.

position.rationale: The detached eastern extension is used as an approximate auditorium location.

negative.statement: The planned expansion would impair school operations and must be taken into account.

position.rationale: Future expansion is not identified; the eastern upper perimeter provides a constrained anchor.

negative.statement: Locating all parking spaces in the basement is disadvantageous for sustainability and construction costs.

position.rationale: Basement parking is below the visible ensemble and approximated beneath the central footprint.

negative.statement: The entire area is occupied, leaving little scope for development.

position.rationale: The distributed masses occupy most of the sampled site, especially toward the eastern edge.

negative.statement: The classrooms are divided into four parts, losing the spatial proximity and diversity expected of a sustainable school.

position.rationale: Classroom subdivision is approximated within the elongated upper school bar.
